name: PromptSource (Prompt Templating Language + Repository)
executive_summary: A formal templating language for data-linked prompts, plus a community repository, defining precisely what a 'prompt template' is as a reusable, parameterized artifact tied to a dataset schema.
description: Defines templates as jinja-style transformations from a dataset's fields into a prompt string plus a corresponding target-output transformation, enabling a single template to be applied across every row of a dataset. Published alongside a repository of thousands of community-contributed templates across many datasets, making it the nearest formal specification in the literature for what a portable, dataset-linked prompt template actually is.
when_to_use: Building a template that needs to be applied programmatically across every row of a structured dataset, not just used once by hand.
when_not_to_use: A single hand-written prompt with no dataset-linked reuse requirement.
known_pitfalls: Template quality still varies a great deal across a large community-contributed repository; not every published template is well-designed.

primary_source.authors: Bach, Sanh, Yong, Webson, Raffel, Nayak, Sharma, Kim, Bari, Fevry, Alyafeai, et al.
primary_source.title: PromptSource: An Integrated Development Environment and Repository for Natural Language Prompts
